items.statement_en: The mode decoding unit turns the choice of numeric format into a set of control signals, so one datapath covers several low-precision floating point formats instead of one conversion pipeline per format.
evidence_quotes: By using control signals generated by the mode decoding unit to govern exponent handling, mantissa alignment, scaling, and accumulation behavior, optimized hardware can execute vector-matrix and matrix-matrix operations more efficiently, across a range of compact numeric formats without requiring separate conversion pipelines or dedicated cores for each format.
The streaming operand provided to CIM macro **101** can be represented in FP8, FP6 or FP4 format and the stationary operand stored in CIM macro **101** can be represented in FP6 or FP4 format.

items.statement_en: Selecting zero at the multiplexers is the mechanism that lets one physical column cell run a narrower weight format on hardware sized for a wider one.
evidence_quotes: To utilize the column cell **220** with the same configuration and design to compute in both mode 1 (weight value in FP6 (1-3-2) format) and mode 2 (weight value in FP4 (1-2-1) format) as listed in Table 1, multiplexers can be used to select zero or W0<0> bit in the FP6 (1-3-2) and select zero or the partial products generated from the W0<0> bit, depending on which mode and data formats are used in the computation.

items.statement_en: Because the exponent addition happens inside the column cell, the accelerator does not need an external exponent tree and moves less data to produce the exponent of a primitive product.
evidence_quotes: By flexibly steering these intermediate signals through configurable paths, the CIM array can generate exponent bits of primitive products efficiently and in place, reducing the need for external exponent trees, minimizing data movement, and enabling support for multiple low-precision numeric formats while maintaining high throughput during VMM operations.

items.statement_en: The paired bitcell is a double buffer: the next weight matrix is written into one bitcell of each memory cell while the current weight matrix is still driving the multiply.
evidence_quotes: Furthermore, the CIM macro **101** can support for a double-buffer scheme (e.g., each memory cell having double bitcells) allowing concurrent loading of the next matrix of weight values while the previous weight values are still in use for the VMM computation.
The CIM macro is further configured to perform, in parallel, a write operation to the first set of bitcells and the VMM operation in the second set of bitcells based on a weight select signal.

items.statement_en: Sizing the column cell by the least common multiple of the supported exponent widths is what makes a single array fit every format in the family without leaving cells unused.
evidence_quotes: The method may also size the number of bitcells in the column based on the least common multiple of supported exponent bit widths for activations and weights, which can help avoid under-utilized cells and may make the layout scalable as more numeric formats are added.
As shown in FIG. **29**, the common cell **220** includes 12 columns and 12 rows, where number 12 is the least common multiple of number 4, 3, and 2.

items.statement_en: Accumulation stays in the integer domain and the conversion back to floating point happens once at the output, not once per multiply.
evidence_quotes: a second part having a synthesizable (or custom) adder tree **426** (see FIG. **4**) that accumulates the element-wise product in the integer domain (e.g., INT 35 and INT5 in Table 1).

These integer values of the VMM product along with the activation values and the scaling factors are inputs to the dequantization unit **106** that is responsible for normalizing the VMM product to FP22 format, where results are output by the output register **108**.

items.statement_en: The same partial-product logic covers subnormal operands, because a normality bit computed from the exponent bits replaces the implicit leading one.
evidence_quotes: As such, the same logic circuits of the column cell **220** can handle both normal and subnormal FP numbers.
Without leading bit “1”, the number of mantissa bits of the primitive products for the activation value Act 0 FP 8 (1-4-3) and the weight value Wdata 0 FP6 (1-3-2) can be reduced to 5 bits.

items.statement_en: Weight reuse is what makes the write path affordable: one loaded weight set can serve many VMM operations, and the specification asserts that full utilization of the compute engine is possible in some embodiments.
evidence_quotes: For example, a single set of weight values may be used for 256 VMM operations before a new set of weight values is needed.
In some embodiments, 100% utilization of the compute engine **100** may be possible.

items.statement_en: All three independent claims are drawn to the same exponent-path structure - one half adder plus three multiplexers that can each select zero - and the format flexibility is claimed through the arithmetic mode that drives those selections rather than through any format-specific circuit.
evidence_quotes: wherein the first multiplexer, the second multiplexer and the third multiplexer perform respective selections based on control signals according to the arithmetic mode.

items.statement_en: The scan path reuses the weight bitcells themselves, so the weight-storage and compute paths can be tested without a separate test structure alongside them.
evidence_quotes: In some embodiments, the methods also encompass operating the CIM macro in different functional and scan modes, performing parallel write and compute operations on different sets of bitcells, and using scan control signals to test or diagnose the weight-storage and compute paths while preserving normal performance characteristics during heavy training and inference workloads.

items.statement_en: The macro interface width follows directly from the vector length and the per-element format width: 32 activation signals of 8 bits and 32 weight signals of 6 bits in the worked example.
evidence_quotes: Each of the activation data signal act0, act1, . . . , act31 has 8 bits with a total 256 bits in one set of activation data signals act0, act1, . . . , act31.
Each of the weight data signals wgt0, wgt1, wgt2, . . . , wgt31 has 6 bits, for a total of 192 bits in one set of weight data signals wgt0, wgt1, wgt2, . . . , wgt31.

items.statement_en: The format flexibility is enumerated rather than open ended: the specification works through a fixed table of activation and weight format pairs and describes how the bits of each lower format are mapped onto the wide-format bit positions.
evidence_quotes: For example, Act<2> in Table 2 can be an output from a multiplexer with 4 inputs connected to bit FP8<2> in modes 1 and 2, to bit FP6<1> in modes 3 and 4, to bit FP6<2> in modes 5 and 6 and to bit FP4<0> in modes 7 and 8.
The streaming operand provided to CIM macro **101** can be represented in FP8, FP6 or FP4 format and the stationary operand stored in CIM macro **101** can be represented in FP6 or FP4 format.

items.background_problem: The background describes accelerators that move activations and weights back and forth between a higher-precision floating point domain and a lower-precision integer datapath, where every conversion step needs its own scaling, rounding and saturation logic and adds area, power and latency while accumulating quantization error across layers.
items.asserted_effect: The disclosure asserts that a compute-in-memory macro whose arithmetic mode is supplied by a mode decoding unit can execute vector-matrix and matrix-matrix operations across a range of compact numeric formats without requiring separate conversion pipelines or dedicated cores for each format.
items.delta: No performance figure is given for this comparison. The asserted difference is structural: format handling is moved into the column cell datapath and its control signals instead of into conversion hardware placed in front of the array.
quotes: Each conversion step requires additional scaling, rounding, and saturation logic, which adds area, power, and latency to already dense compute fabrics, and can introduce cumulative quantization errors that degrade numerical behavior over many layers.

By using control signals generated by the mode decoding unit to govern exponent handling, mantissa alignment, scaling, and accumulation behavior, optimized hardware can execute vector-matrix and matrix-matrix operations more efficiently, across a range of compact numeric formats without requiring separate conversion pipelines or dedicated cores for each format.

items.background_problem: The background states that as new low-bit floating point encodings appear, fixed conversion pipelines and format-specific data paths become increasingly difficult to adapt, which limits the models and deployment scenarios the hardware can serve.
items.asserted_effect: The disclosure asserts that different activation and weight format combinations can be chosen to balance accuracy, memory bandwidth and power consumption while the external programming model stays consistent and the underlying storage arrays, arithmetic structures and dataflow are not significantly redesigned.
items.delta: The delta offered is again structural rather than quantified: the same column cell is reused across format pairs by selecting zero at the multiplexers, and the cell is sized once from the least common multiple of the supported exponent widths so that later formats fit the existing pattern.
quotes: As new low-bit formats and variants are introduced to improve efficiency (such as different 8-bit or sub-8-bit floating-point encodings), fixed conversion pipelines and format-specific data paths become increasingly difficult to adapt, limiting the flexibility of the hardware to support evolving models and deployment scenarios.

Additionally, this flexible support allows, for example, different combinations of formats for activations and weights to be employed to balance accuracy, memory bandwidth, and power consumption, while preserving a consistent external programming model and avoiding significant redesign of underlying storage arrays, arithmetic structures, or dataflow for new or evolving numeric schemes.

The method may also size the number of bitcells in the column based on the least common multiple of supported exponent bit widths for activations and weights, which can help avoid under-utilized cells and may make the layout scalable as more numeric formats are added.

items.background_problem: The disclosure frames the baseline as one in which the exponent bits of a floating point product are formed outside the memory array, which requires external exponent trees and the data movement needed to feed them.
items.asserted_effect: The disclosure asserts that generating exponent bits of primitive products in place, by steering carry and sum information through configurable paths inside the column cell, reduces the need for external exponent trees and minimizes data movement while maintaining high throughput during VMM operations.
items.delta: No measured reduction in area, energy or latency is stated. The stated difference is that the exponent adder chain sits inside the column cell next to the weight bitcells, and that the same chain is re-steered by control signals rather than replaced when the format changes.
quotes: By flexibly steering these intermediate signals through configurable paths, the CIM array can generate exponent bits of primitive products efficiently and in place, reducing the need for external exponent trees, minimizing data movement, and enabling support for multiple low-precision numeric formats while maintaining high throughput during VMM operations.
In summary, the compute engine **100** admits data in the MXFP format and performs a VMM operation, returning data (dequantized dot products) in a custom precision format (e.g., FP22).
